articles.body_text: Las regiones del país tienen oportunidades para atraer inversiones en sectores como la agroindustria, minería, industria y turismo. Sin embargo, aprovechar ese potencial requiere resolver problemas estructurales que siguen restándoles competitividad. La inseguridad, la falta de conectividad, los altos costos de energía y las brechas de infraestructura fueron algunos de los obstáculos que expusieron los representantes de las cámaras de comercio de La Libertad, Huancayo, Loreto y Cusco durante el segundo día de CADE Ejecutivos 2026. La Libertad, por ejemplo, es la tercera región con mayor aporte al PBI nacional y lidera la producción de oro y la agroindustria. Además, en la macrorregión norte existe la posibilidad de ampliar la frontera agraria mediante proyectos como Chavimochic, Olmos y Alto Piura, que permitirían incorporar nuevas tierras a la actividad agrícola y generar entre 200,000 y 300,000 puestos de trabajo formales. A estas oportunidades se suma la posibilidad de incrementar la producción petrolera a 150.000 barriles diarios, explicó Fernando Guerra, presidente de la Cámara de Comercio de La Libertad. No obstante, el principal obstáculo para el desarrollo de la zona es la inseguridad, un problema que no solo afecta a La Libertad, sino a todo el norte peruano, sostuvo. “Nosotros los gremios del norte estamos listos para seguir aportando vía obras por impuestos y servicios por impuestos para darle esa inteligencia, esa tecnología, esa infraestructura que necesita la policía, el Ministerio Público, así como el Poder Judicial. Pero necesitamos un liderazgo firme”, mencionó Guerra. En la macrorregión centro, las oportunidades pasan por descentralizar la actividad industrial y aprovechar el potencial turístico de sus regiones. Así lo planteó José Luis García, presidente de la Cámara de Comercio de Huancayo, quien cuestionó la concentración de la industria en Lima y la falta de conectividad para impulsar su desarrollo en provincias como Huánuco, Pasco, Ayacucho, Huancavelica y Junín. También advirtió sobre la necesidad de promover el turismo en zonas con una amplia oferta de festividades. A estos problemas se suman las trabas burocráticas de las municipalidades, que frenan el desarrollo empresarial. Por su parte, la macrorregión oriente enfrenta brechas que limitan el aprovechamiento de sus recursos. Jorge Morales, presidente de la Cámara de Comercio de Loreto, descartó que la Amazonía sea una región pobre. A su juicio, el problema es que está “desconectada, desatendida y subaprovechada”. Como muestra de esta situación, señaló que Loreto reporta un 62% de anemia infantil y que 8 de cada 10 niños no comprenden lo que leen. Además, esta misma proporción tampoco puede resolver problemas matemáticos. Frente a este escenario, mejorar la calidad de vida en el oriente peruano pasa por atender dos necesidades fundamentales: reducir el alto costo de la energía y fortalecer la conectividad. “Cómo podemos hacer empresas si no tenemos energía. Loreto paga la energía más cara del Perú, y tenemos también una energía pésima en San Martín. Tenemos que mejorarla. Queremos conectarnos al Sistema Eléctrico Integrado Nacional, pero no tenemos más que proyectos”, refirió. En el sur, el principal cuestionamiento apunta a que la riqueza que genera la región no se traduce necesariamente en bienestar ni en mejores condiciones para el desarrollo empresarial. Fernando Santoyo, presidente de la Cámara de Comercio de Cusco, sostuvo que uno de los problemas que resta competitividad a esta zona es el elevado costo de la energía, pese a que allí se produce gas. “Cerca del 45% de la energía nacional proviene de Camisea. Pero, ¿cuánto de eso le beneficia al sur? Todavía tenemos representación parlamentaria y algunas organizaciones sociales que se oponen a la masificación del gas. En el sur pagamos 20% más del precio de la energía comparado con Lima y con muchas regiones de la costa. Y en cuanto a gas, pagamos tres veces más el tener GLP y no poder disfrutar todavía del gas natural. Así cualquier empresa es poco competitiva”, refirió. Más allá de las condiciones particulares de cada macrorregión, la falta de infraestructura y conectividad sigue siendo uno de los principales obstáculos para elevar la competitividad. En ese contexto, los representantes de las cámaras de comercio de Huancayo y Loreto dirigieron sus cuestionamientos al ministro de Transportes y Comunicaciones, Angello Tangherlini, quien participó en la primera jornada de CADE, y solicitaron precisiones sobre el avance de diversos proyectos. García puso especial énfasis en las omisiones que, a su juicio, tuvo el funcionario durante su presentación, entre ellas la falta de plazos y presupuesto para la ejecución de la Carretera Central. “Para nosotros la ecuación conectividad y competitividad es válida. No nos posterguen. No es modo de reclamo. Ayer el ministro del MTC expuso importantes proyectos, pero no dio plazos. Entonces, el proyecto de ley respecto a la nueva carretera central es declarativa, no está reglamentada y tampoco tiene presupuesto. Entonces, no tenemos nada. Vamos a insistir en ello, por supuesto, porque si hablamos de industrialización, ¿cómo reducimos costos a todos los sectores que requieren no solamente la carretera central, sino vías de penetración?”, cuestionó. Desde Loreto, Morales recordó la necesidad de concretar la Hidrovía Amazónica, considerada un eje central del corredor logístico bioceánico conectado con Chancay. Sin embargo, lamentó que el proyecto continúe sin avances. “La Hidrovía hasta ahora duerme el sueño de los justos, pese a todo el tema de Chancay. Hay que mirar de una u otra manera la forma cómo tenemos que conectarnos. Si hablamos del costo logístico: el marítimo fluvial es uno, ferroviario es cuatro. El carretero es nueve, pero con las carreteras como están en el Perú llega a 11”, resaltó. En el norte, Guerra también cuestionó la paralización de la Red Vial 4 y la Autopista del Sol, cuya construcción, tras 17 años, registra apenas un 60% de avance. La culminación de ambos proyectos no solo elevaría la competitividad de esta zona, sino que también permitiría a la macrorregión aprovechar al máximo el desarrollo del Megapuerto de Chancay. “Queremos pedir al Estado que declaren emergencia y que ponga de interés nacional la consecución, ejecución y culminación de ese proyecto es muy importante para el norte y para la sostenibilidad económica de nuestra macrorregión”, mencionó. El sur también puso sobre la mesa sus demandas en materia de infraestructura. Una de las principales es la carretera del Circuito Valle Sagrado, cuyo deterioro contrasta con el volumen de visitantes que recibe: más de 1.5 millones de turistas anuales. “¿Qué está haciendo el Ministerio de Transportes para solucionar ese problema por donde circula más de 1 millón y medio de turistas al año? Estamos 2 años padeciendo de una vía que no responde a la categoría del Cusco y del Perú en cuanto a prestación y presencia de servicios turísticos”, destacó.

articles.title: Mexicanas marchan en Ciudad de México para alzar la voz contra las violencias machistas
articles.summary: Día Internacional de la Eliminación de la Violencia contra la Mujer | Las mexicanas volvieron este miércoles a las calles de Ciudad de México para alzar la voz contra las violencias machistas en un país donde siete de cada diez mujeres de 15 años o más han sufrido algún tipo de violencia a lo largo de su vida.
articles.body_text: Las mexicanas volvieron este miércoles a las calles de Ciudad de México para alzar la voz contra las violencias machistas en un país donde siete de cada diez mujeres de 15 años o más han sufrido algún tipo de violencia a lo largo de su vida. “¡No llegamos todas mientras una mujer siga viviendo en violencia!” es la consigna de la marcha convocada por la Coordinación 8M en este Día Internacional de la Eliminación de la Violencia contra las Mujeres. La marcha partió de la Glorieta de las Mujeres que Luchan, sobre Paseo de la Reforma, rumbo al Zócalo, a poco más de dos años de la llegada de Claudia Sheinbaum, la primera mujer en ocupar la Presidencia de México. En 2025, el primer año completo de Sheinbaum como presidenta, México registró 3.338 asesinatos de mujeres, un promedio de nueve al día, frente a los 3.739 de 2024, según cifras del Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Geografía (Inegi). La convocatoria situó al frente de la marcha a familiares de víctimas de feminicidio y desaparición, así como a sobrevivientes de violencia machista, seguidas de colectivas feministas, mujeres indígenas, colectivos de la diversidad sexogenérica, estudiantes, sindicatos y organizaciones de la sociedad civil. Entre las principales demandas se encuentran el fin de los feminicidios, la presentación con vida de las personas desaparecidas, la tipificación del feminicidio en grado de tentativa y el cese de la criminalización de la protesta feminista. “Este 25N: no queremos más moños naranjas. Queremos decisiones claras y contundentes para combatir la violencia”, señaló en un comunicado Lizeth Mejorada, vocera de Mujeres Vivas, Mujeres Libres, organización que exige eliminar el aborto de los códigos penales federal y capitalino. Horas antes de la movilización, las autoridades colocaron vallas para resguardar el Palacio Nacional, sede del Ejecutivo federal. La protesta coincide con la presentación este miércoles de la campaña Hombres por la Transformación, en la que el Gobierno federal plantea doce compromisos para involucrar a los hombres en la prevención de las violencias machistas y combatir los estereotipos de género. Las movilizaciones por el 25N, convocadas también en estados como Nuevo León, Jalisco, Durango y Estado de México, marcan el inicio de los 16 días de activismo contra la violencia de género, que culminarán el 10 de diciembre, Día de los Derechos Humanos. En dos décadas, los feminicidios en México aumentaron un 44,3 % y el uso de armas de fuego en los homicidios de mujeres casi se duplicó, al pasar del 31,6 % en 2006 al 62,1 %, según un informe publicado este miércoles por la organización Data Cívica. La ONG también documentó un aumento en las desapariciones de mujeres y niñas, de 12.496 en 2023 a 13.610 en 2025. Entre el 1 de enero y el 20 de octubre de 2026 se registraron otras 7.216. Además, el 70,1 % de las mexicanas de 15 años o más en México ha experimentado algún tipo de violencia a lo largo de su vida: el 51,6 % violencia psicológica y el 49,7 %, sexual, según una encuesta del Inegi de 2021.

articles.title: Piura: MTC atiende emergencia vial por crecida en la quebrada Sol Sol
articles.summary: Provías Nacional habilitó el tránsito en el badén Sol Sol, en Morropón, Piura tras el colapso de un desvío por lluvias y crecida del río.
articles.body_text: El Ministerio de Transportes y Comunicaciones (MTC), a través de Provías Nacional, activó la atención de una emergencia vial en el badén Sol Sol, en la provincia de Morropón, departamento de Piura, debido a las lluvias intensas, consiguiendo habilitar el tránsito vehicular en la zona. Provías Nacional ejecutó trabajos de emergencia que comprendieron la colocación de roca y material, con el objetivo de recuperar las condiciones de transitabilidad y restablecer el paso por este badén en el transcurso del día. Las labores se desarrollan como parte de la atención inmediata de la afectación ocasionada por las condiciones climáticas y el incremento del caudal del río, priorizando la recuperación de la conectividad para los usuarios de la ruta. El Ministerio de Transportes y Comunicaciones (MTC),exhorta a la población a evitar transitar por este sector mientras se ejecutan los trabajos y hasta que las condiciones de seguridad se restablezcan. Provías Nacional informó que continuará con las acciones necesarias para atender esta emergencia vial y recuperar la transitabilidad en el sector afectado. El Servicio Nacional de Meteorología e Hidrología del Perú (Senamhi) atribuyó la crecida a las intensas precipitaciones en la cuenca hidrográfica. Debido a esta acumulación de agua, la cuenca cambió rápidamente de categoría y pasó del umbral amarillo al nivel de alerta naranja en pocas horas. El organismo de emergencia advirtió que la crecida del caudal amenazó con inundar al menos quince centros poblados de la provincia de Paita y zonas aledañas. Entre las localidades expuestas a sufrir daños figuraron Amotape, Miramar, San Jorge, Rinconada, Paredones, San Felipe de Vichayal, Tamarindo, Vichayal, Salitral, Sojo, Marcavelica, Tangarara y Querecotillo. El incremento de la corriente coincidió con la emisión de boletines oficiales que situaron a la región en nivel de peligro rojo por lluvias intensas. Las alertas vigentes del Senamhi consideraron un alto riesgo de activación de quebradas en las provincias piuranas de Ayabaca, Huancabamba, Morropón, Paita, Sullana y Talara.

articles.title: CADE Ejecutivos 2026: regiones reclaman seguridad, conectividad y energía barata
articles.summary: Las regiones del país tienen oportunidades para atraer inversiones en sectores como la agroindustria, minería, industria y turismo. Sin embargo, aprovechar ese potencial requiere resolver problemas estructurales que siguen restándoles competitividad. La inseguridad, la falta de conectividad, los altos costos de energía y las brechas de infraestructura fueron algunos de los obstáculos que expusieron los representantes de las cámaras de comercio de La Libertad, Huancayo, Loreto y Cusco durante el segundo día de CADE Ejecutivos 2026.
articles.body_text: Las regiones del país tienen oportunidades para atraer inversiones en sectores como la agroindustria, minería, industria y turismo. Sin embargo, aprovechar ese potencial requiere resolver problemas estructurales que siguen restándoles competitividad. La inseguridad, la falta de conectividad, los altos costos de energía y las brechas de infraestructura fueron algunos de los obstáculos que expusieron los representantes de las cámaras de comercio de La Libertad, Huancayo, Loreto y Cusco durante el segundo día de CADE Ejecutivos 2026. La Libertad, por ejemplo, es la tercera región con mayor aporte al PBI nacional y lidera la producción de oro y la agroindustria. Además, en la macrorregión norte existe la posibilidad de ampliar la frontera agraria mediante proyectos como Chavimochic, Olmos y Alto Piura, que permitirían incorporar nuevas tierras a la actividad agrícola y generar entre 200,000 y 300,000 puestos de trabajo formales. A estas oportunidades se suma la posibilidad de incrementar la producción petrolera a 150.000 barriles diarios, explicó Fernando Guerra, presidente de la Cámara de Comercio de La Libertad. No obstante, el principal obstáculo para el desarrollo de la zona es la inseguridad, un problema que no solo afecta a La Libertad, sino a todo el norte peruano, sostuvo. “Nosotros los gremios del norte estamos listos para seguir aportando vía obras por impuestos y servicios por impuestos para darle esa inteligencia, esa tecnología, esa infraestructura que necesita la policía, el Ministerio Público, así como el Poder Judicial. Pero necesitamos un liderazgo firme”, mencionó Guerra. En la macrorregión centro, las oportunidades pasan por descentralizar la actividad industrial y aprovechar el potencial turístico de sus regiones. Así lo planteó José Luis García, presidente de la Cámara de Comercio de Huancayo, quien cuestionó la concentración de la industria en Lima y la falta de conectividad para impulsar su desarrollo en provincias como Huánuco, Pasco, Ayacucho, Huancavelica y Junín. También advirtió sobre la necesidad de promover el turismo en zonas con una amplia oferta de festividades. A estos problemas se suman las trabas burocráticas de las municipalidades, que frenan el desarrollo empresarial. Por su parte, la macrorregión oriente enfrenta brechas que limitan el aprovechamiento de sus recursos. Jorge Morales, presidente de la Cámara de Comercio de Loreto, descartó que la Amazonía sea una región pobre. A su juicio, el problema es que está “desconectada, desatendida y subaprovechada”. Como muestra de esta situación, señaló que Loreto reporta un 62% de anemia infantil y que 8 de cada 10 niños no comprenden lo que leen. Además, esta misma proporción tampoco puede resolver problemas matemáticos. Frente a este escenario, mejorar la calidad de vida en el oriente peruano pasa por atender dos necesidades fundamentales: reducir el alto costo de la energía y fortalecer la conectividad. “Cómo podemos hacer empresas si no tenemos energía. Loreto paga la energía más cara del Perú, y tenemos también una energía pésima en San Martín. Tenemos que mejorarla. Queremos conectarnos al Sistema Eléctrico Integrado Nacional, pero no tenemos más que proyectos”, refirió. En el sur, el principal cuestionamiento apunta a que la riqueza que genera la región no se traduce necesariamente en bienestar ni en mejores condiciones para el desarrollo empresarial. Fernando Santoyo, presidente de la Cámara de Comercio de Cusco, sostuvo que uno de los problemas que resta competitividad a esta zona es el elevado costo de la energía, pese a que allí se produce gas. “Cerca del 45% de la energía nacional proviene de Camisea. Pero, ¿cuánto de eso le beneficia al sur? Todavía tenemos representación parlamentaria y algunas organizaciones sociales que se oponen a la masificación del gas. En el sur pagamos 20% más del precio de la energía comparado con Lima y con muchas regiones de la costa. Y en cuanto a gas, pagamos tres veces más el tener GLP y no poder disfrutar todavía del gas natural. Así cualquier empresa es poco competitiva”, refirió. Más allá de las condiciones particulares de cada macrorregión, la falta de infraestructura y conectividad sigue siendo uno de los principales obstáculos para elevar la competitividad. En ese contexto, los representantes de las cámaras de comercio de Huancayo y Loreto dirigieron sus cuestionamientos al ministro de Transportes y Comunicaciones, Angello Tangherlini, quien participó en la primera jornada de CADE, y solicitaron precisiones sobre el avance de diversos proyectos. García puso especial énfasis en las omisiones que, a su juicio, tuvo el funcionario durante su presentación, entre ellas la falta de plazos y presupuesto para la ejecución de la Carretera Central. “Para nosotros la ecuación conectividad y competitividad es válida. No nos posterguen. No es modo de reclamo. Ayer el ministro del MTC expuso importantes proyectos, pero no dio plazos. Entonces, el proyecto de ley respecto a la nueva carretera central es declarativa, no está reglamentada y tampoco tiene presupuesto. Entonces, no tenemos nada. Vamos a insistir en ello, por supuesto, porque si hablamos de industrialización, ¿cómo reducimos costos a todos los sectores que requieren no solamente la carretera central, sino vías de penetración?”, cuestionó. Desde Loreto, Morales recordó la necesidad de concretar la Hidrovía Amazónica, considerada un eje central del corredor logístico bioceánico conectado con Chancay. Sin embargo, lamentó que el proyecto continúe sin avances. “La Hidrovía hasta ahora duerme el sueño de los justos, pese a todo el tema de Chancay. Hay que mirar de una u otra manera la forma cómo tenemos que conectarnos. Si hablamos del costo logístico: el marítimo fluvial es uno, ferroviario es cuatro. El carretero es nueve, pero con las carreteras como están en el Perú llega a 11”, resaltó. En el norte, Guerra también cuestionó la paralización de la Red Vial 4 y la Autopista del Sol, cuya construcción, tras 17 años, registra apenas un 60% de avance. La culminación de ambos proyectos no solo elevaría la competitividad de esta zona, sino que también permitiría a la macrorregión aprovechar al máximo el desarrollo del Megapuerto de Chancay. “Queremos pedir al Estado que declaren emergencia y que ponga de interés nacional la consecución, ejecución y culminación de ese proyecto es muy importante para el norte y para la sostenibilidad económica de nuestra macrorregión”, mencionó. El sur también puso sobre la mesa sus demandas en materia de infraestructura. Una de las principales es la carretera del Circuito Valle Sagrado, cuyo deterioro contrasta con el volumen de visitantes que recibe: más de 1.5 millones de turistas anuales. “¿Qué está haciendo el Ministerio de Transportes para solucionar ese problema por donde circula más de 1 millón y medio de turistas al año? articles.title: Tumbes: Oleaje anómalo dañó viviendas, hoteles y restaurantes en balneario de Zorritos
articles.summary: El oleaje anómalo que azotó las costas de Tumbes durante cinco días provocó daños en viviendas, hoteles y restaurantes del balneario de Zorritos, ubicado en la provincia de Contralmirante Villar.
articles.body_text: El oleaje anómalo que azotó las costas de Tumbes durante cinco días provocó daños en viviendas, hoteles y restaurantes del balneario de Zorritos, ubicado en la provincia de Contralmirante Villar. Según informó Canal N, gran parte de la infraestructura hotelera y restaurantes de zonas turísticas quedó destruida por las olas, que han socavado las bases de diversas construcciones ubicadas cerca de la orilla. Según las primeras informaciones de las autoridades, serían más de 30 los hospedajes, hoteles, restaurantes e infraestructuras turísticas que han sido duramente afectados por las olas en el balneario. Se prevé que la intensidad del oleaje disminuya entre este lunes y martes. Sin embargo, parte de la infraestructura turística presenta daños considerables debido a la magnitud del oleaje. El mar se había retirado cerca de 400 metros de su antigua línea costera. Con el oleaje, ha retornado a sus límites anteriores, afectando a quienes construyeron establecimientos turísticos en la zona libre. Debido a esta situación, propietarios de hoteles y restaurantes colocaron rocas y geobolsas para proteger sus instalaciones de las olas, pero recibieron un llamado de atención de la Capitanía de Puerto. La autoridad marítima sostiene que la colocación de rocas puede desviar el impacto de las olas hacia otros sectores que no cuentan con protección, lo que podría generar mayores daños en el balneario.

articles.title: Ica: Se esperan lluvias superiores a sus valores normales entre enero y marzo de 2027
articles.summary: El Servicio Nacional de Meteorología e Hidrología del Perú (Senamhi) informó que entre enero y marzo de 2027 se esperan lluvias superiores a sus valores habituales en la región Ica.
articles.body_text: El Servicio Nacional de Meteorología e Hidrología del Perú (Senamhi) informó que entre enero y marzo de 2027 se esperan lluvias superiores a sus valores habituales en la región Ica. Según el organismo adscrito al Ministerio del Ambiente (Minam), estas condiciones podrían generar un incremento de los caudales de los ríos Ica, Pisco y San Juan, así como aumentar el riesgo de inundaciones y activación de quebradas. Ante este escenario, que podría manifestarse desde diciembre, la Dirección Zonal 5 (DZ 5) del Senamhi mantiene una vigilancia permanente de las condiciones meteorológicas para proporcionar información especializada que contribuya a proteger a la ciudadanía, las viviendas, la infraestructura y las actividades productivas. Durante una sesión ordinaria del Consejo Regional de Ica, el especialista del Senamhi Sergio Mitma explicó que el monitoreo comprende también las provincias de Huaytará y Castrovirreyna, en Huancavelica, y Lucanas, en Ayacucho. Detalló que las precipitaciones en las partes altas de las cuencas inciden en el comportamiento de los caudales de los ríos que atraviesan el departamento de Ica. De acuerdo con el Comunicado Oficial N.° 20-2026 de la Comisión Multisectorial encargada del Estudio Nacional del Fenómeno El Niño (Enfen), persisten condiciones cálidas en la temperatura superficial del mar, asociadas al incremento de las temperaturas diurnas y nocturnas registrado durante los últimos meses en la zona costera de Ica, con anomalías de entre 3 y 6 °C. Por su parte, el Comunicado Oficial N.° 19-2026 del Enfen señala que El Niño mantendría una magnitud extraordinaria hasta febrero de 2027, con una disminución gradual durante los meses posteriores.

articles.summary: The credit rating agency may lower Nvidia's credit rating to AA-, the fourth-highest rating.
articles.body_text: S&P Global Ratings, one of the three major credit rating agencies, is considering downgrading Nvidia’s rating, citing concerns about the company’s management and governance practices. Despite Nvidia’s strong financial performance, the ouster and reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang has raised concerns about “weak executive oversight and lack of succession planning” and “key man risk,” meaning heavy reliance on Huang for its future success, S&P said in a statement . The agency expects to finish its review within 90 days and could cut Nvidia’s rating from AA to AA-, the fourth-highest on its scale. Although Nvidia is certain to keep its investment-grade rating, a downgrade could raise its borrowing costs. Because Nvidia backstops neoclouds and other infrastructure companies that lack strong credit on their own, a lower rating could make their debt costlier or force them to post more collateral. In August, Nvidia announced plans to arrange $500 billion in financing for AI infrastructure with six financial institutions, including Goldman Sachs, Apollo, and Blackstone. Under the original terms, Nvidia would guarantee 25% of the loans. But even before Huang’s ouster and return, lenders had been demanding that Nvidia guarantee more, Bloomberg reported . articles.title: FCC approves SpaceX plan to put AI data centers in space | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The FCC dismissed some of the key concerns raised by opponents, including potential threats to scientific research, because the agency determined they fell outside its regulatory authority.
articles.body_text: SpaceX was given conditional approval by the Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday to deploy and operate a constellation of up to 1 million satellites for its orbital data center business, a regulatory victory for Elon Musk and his bid to move AI data centers into space. The FCC authorization was granted despite objections from Amazon, Viasat, and the American Astronomical Society, which flagged concerns over orbital debris and congestion, radiofrequency interference, and environmental consequences. Amazon, which is building a competitor to SpaceX’s Starlink service, argued in its petition that the application lacked basic details and described it as a “lofty ambition rather than a real plan.” Despite that lack of detail, Amazon also said the proposal “risks real harm.” The FCC dismissed some of the key concerns raised by opponents, including potential threats to scientific research, because the agency determined they fell outside its regulatory authority. FCC Chair Brendan Carr said in a statement that the action “opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America’s leadership and growth.” Musk thanked Carr in a post on X , writing “Much appreciate. This will be a great asset to America and the world.” This initial regulatory approval doesn’t mean orbital data centers are imminent. SpaceX faces a number of technical and economic challenges, including how to dramatically reduce the cost of manufacturing and launching satellites, cool processors in space, and even how to secure financing for chips that are destined for orbit. The company must also clear other regulatory hurdles. The FCC has not yet approved SpaceX’s plans to handle orbital debris for satellites that would operate above 600 kilometers, for instance. SpaceX requested a waiver of existing FCC rules, which requires satellites ending missions below 2,000 kilometers reenter Earth’s atmosphere within five years of completing those missions. The company is interested in moving some of these retired satellites into other orbits around Earth or even around the sun, according to the FCC authorization document . SpaceX has said it plans to deploy the satellites, known as Starmind, at altitudes ranging from 500 to 1,002 kilometers. The FCC’s approval gives SpaceX the authority to use radiofrequency communications to maintain contact with and control its orbital data centers from Earth if their primary communications systems fail. The Starmind satellites would primarily communicate using lasers to connect with other satellites, including SpaceX’s Starlink. The FCC has given SpaceX time to sort out these issues. Under the approval, SpaceX has seven years to get its first operational satellite into orbit and 14 years to deploy the entire constellation. articles.title: Jensen Huang broke Nvidia's code of conduct, and his employees may not forget it | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Most codes of conduct serve as a reflection of corporate culture. In Nvidia's case, that could have consequences.
articles.body_text: When Jensen Huang gave his first all-hands address since returning as CEO, there was an odd emphasis on Nvidia’s code of conduct. He admitted to violating the code, then emphasized that no one was exempt from it. But that “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door,” Huang said, according to Wired . “Facts, circumstances, a lot of assessments” still matter. In other words, the code applies to everyone, but breaking it doesn’t automatically cost anyone their job, including, apparently, the CEO. It’s an awkward stance for a company whose CEO has admitted to breaking its rules. A central part of modern human resources, a code of conduct can seem like a quasi-legal rulebook that lays out unacceptable behavior. But experts say most codes are better understood as a reflection of corporate culture. When an infraction goes unpunished, the main risk isn’t legal but cultural — that employees will feel embarrassed or even angry about the company they work for. That’s the risk Huang now faces at Nvidia. Matt Plass, chief market strategy officer at LRN, an ethics and compliance training outfit, recently surveyed more than 2,000 workers across different industries for a study on workplace codes of conduct . As Plass sees it, the biggest risk is that employees will become ashamed of their workplace. “People coming into the workforce now, ethics is incredibly important to them,” he told TechCrunch. “They’re really mindful of the ethical standards of their company. They’re really embarrassed and angry when senior leadership lets them down.” The consequences of violating the rules aren’t always tangible, but they’re definitely real. Plass gave one example of a company that banned corporate travel to cut costs — only to have its CEO turn up in a VIP box at the Olympics. “For over a decade afterwards, ‘the Olympics’ was used within that company as an example of the worst thing an employee could do. People would say, ‘Yeah, I shouldn’t have done that, but it’s not like I went to the Olympics.’” Plass says companies that remove an executive typically do so after an investigation, then try to win back employees. “In most organizations they make a change at the top based on what’s happened,” he said, “and then they will have a hearts-and-minds initiative, to go out to their employee base and their customers and their investors and everybody else, and say, we get it. We’re sorry. We’ve changed. That’s essentially what they do.” Of course, that playbook is harder to follow at a company like Nvidia, where Huang left without a clear succession plan, and there are serious doubts about whether the company could continue to thrive without him. In cases like that, Plass acknowledges there’s no easy answer. “I would draw a distinction there between the kind of companies where the CEO is a kind of godhead figure … where the person and the company are almost impossible to separate,” he said. “There it’s much, much harder to deal with.” In that context, Huang’s stutter-step over the code of conduct is easier to understand. Judging by the employee campaign for his reinstatement, Huang’s return hasn’t created a morale problem so far. But as the coming months put more pressure on Huang and his colleagues, sidestepping the code could end up costing Nvidia something harder to measure — its employees’ pride in the company. articles.title: The canceled Tesla Cybertruck is the fastest-selling used truck in America | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The Tesla Cybertruck was the fastest-selling used truck last month, averaging just 39.1 days on the market compared to 65.5 days for trucks overall.
articles.body_text: Tesla Cybertruck sales never reached the lofty heights CEO Elon Musk predicted when it launched. But the futuristic, steel-clad EV is finding new life in the used car market, according to analysis of sales figures by iSeeCars.com . The automotive search engine and research platform analyzed more than 1.1 million sales of one- to five-year-old used vehicles in October 2026 and measured the average days on market by drivetrain, vehicle type, and individual model. The upshot: The Tesla Cybertruck was the fastest-selling used truck, averaging just 39.1 days on the market compared with 65.5 days for trucks overall. Used Cybertrucks sold faster than any other truck, including the Ford Maverick Hybrid, which held the No. 2 spot, and the Rivian R1T, in third place. According to iSeeCars.com, the Cybertruck’s sales performance lines up with a broader pattern in the used vehicle market: Used battery electric vehicles are hot sellers right now, with 16 of the 25 fastest-selling used cars fully electric. EVs are even edging out hybrids in terms of average days on market. EVs average 45.6 days on market compared to 54.5 days for hybrids and 61 days for gasoline-powered vehicles. Not every EV is selling well, however. For instance, iSeeCars.com found that the Cadillac Escalade IQ was the slowest-selling vehicle in the study, averaging 134.3 days on the market, more than twice the overall industry average. Karl Brauer, executive analyst at iSeeCars.com, told TechCrunch that high gasoline prices have changed consumer-buying habits, prompting more people to opt for an EV or hybrid over an internal combustion engine vehicle. If high prices persist, as they have since March, that trend could continue. Keep in mind that these were October sales, the month before Musk announced Tesla would stop making the Cybertruck in 2027. Fuel prices and the relative rarity of Cybertrucks in the used car market were driving demand even before the cancellation announcement, Brauer said. “The Cybertruck has only been out for a few years, so you have a lot of used ones coming off lease and entering the used car market for the first time,” he said, adding that used Cybertrucks are cheap relative to their MSRP. The impending cancellation will likely fuel used Cybertruck sales, although the pace may ebb and flow over the next year. “The canceling of the new Cybertruck is making people kind of aware — it’s like, oh wow, these things aren’t going to be coming anymore,” Brauer said. “Whatever demand is for them, supply will not be continuing to grow.” Brauer said that once production of the Cybertruck ends — which is expected in summer 2027 — sales of used versions may pop once again. “When the last one is being produced, that’ll probably reignite things again, and for a few months after that,” he said. In a long X post on Wednesday, Amodei called the suggestion “absurd.” “We should never sacrifice legitimacy or self-determination at the altar of efficiency or security,” he wrote. This argument against autocracy applies word for word against governance by AI, and I feel equally strongly that turning over governance to AI is a bad idea…No one who had carefully read my writing or my interviews could reasonably conclude that I believe anything different.” The statement comes after a growing chorus from Anthropic rivals suggesting that human agency could be at risk if AI is developed irresponsibly. Earlier this month, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said he wanted to ensure people continue to have “agency over the future.” Meta’s chief AI officer Alexandr Wang also wrote in an essay on X that we “should not be okay with a ‘handover’ of society to AI.” “It is hard to imagine a world where humanity can maintain control over fully unconstrained recursive self-improvement,” Wang wrote. “Now that we are at a point where the scientific and technical problems on capability progress are likely solved, we must not only make progress in the extremely urgent areas of safety, alignment, and security, but we have to start thinking through how we progress thoughtfully.” But in published essays, Amodei claims he has repeatedly advocated for democratic oversight of AI, saying the technology should strengthen democratic institutions and that humans should retain ultimate decision-making power. Amodei noted that there’s a difference between surrendering human free will broadly and the idea that “as AI systems advance, they become capable of doing specific tasks in a more automated way.” As examples, he gave AI driving a car, designing a cancer drug, or writing end-to-end software. Amodei suggested drawing a line at recursive self-improvement (RSI), or AI that can improve itself without human assistance. Many safety experts see RSI as inevitably leading to a loss of human control, a point Amodei implicitly acknowledged, writing, “we may want limits on this process.” Still, Anthropic is laying the groundwork for RSI by incorporating AI into an increasing share of its own research and development. The company said in June that Claude authored more than 80% of the code merged into Anthropic’s codebase. An independent assessment published this month by AI safety research nonprofit METR found that Anthropic’s models are improving at about twice their historical rate, primarily driven by AI-assisted research. In its own IPO filings, Anthropic describes how each successive generation of Claude accelerates the development of the next, a process it refers to as “closing the loop.” “As we said publicly in early November, we don’t expect it to be safe for Claude to build successive frontier models fully autonomously, without meaningful human supervision or understanding,” Amodei wrote. The problem with “meaningful human supervision or understanding” is that AI is already advancing faster than engineers and safety experts can fully audit it, leaving them increasingly reliant on other AI systems to act as judge and jury. The issue compounds when AI models engage in deceptive behavior, particularly when they recognize they’re being evaluated, making them harder to trust and control.

articles.title: 1Password said hackers broke into its internal systems, but customer passwords are safe | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The password manager maker said an attacker gained access to an employee's corporate account and took some information about customers.
articles.body_text: Password manager maker 1Password has confirmed that some customer information was taken in a recent intrusion into its internal systems, but that customer password vaults and other secrets were not accessed. The Toronto-based tech company said in a blog post published Wednesday that it detected an intrusion on November 19, in which an attacker gained access to an employee’s corporate account with GitHub, which the company uses to share and store its source code. The attacker used that employee’s access to push malicious code to the company’s internal servers, which allowed the hacker to download some data about 1Password customers, including their names and the email address that they use for logging into their account. The company said that the attacker also took details about when a 1Password account was created and when a user last logged in. 1Password said that customer vaults, which store their passwords, were “at no point” available to the attacker. The company also said that it doesn’t have access to customer account passwords or their secret keys, which are used to scramble their passwords so that 1Password cannot see them. In addition, the company said that its apps and extensions are unaffected by the incident. It’s unclear how the attacker gained access to the employee’s corporate account, and a spokesperson for 1Password did not immediately respond to TechCrunch’s questions about the incident. 1Password did not say whether it had notified customers whose information was taken in the breach, or how many customers had information taken. We’ve also asked if the company has received any communication or demands from the hackers. We’ll update if we hear back from 1Password. The company touts millions of customers and more than 200,000 businesses who use its password manager products to store their passwords, credentials, payment card information, and more. Security experts have long recommended password managers as a better way of generating stronger credentials and keeping track of online accounts. articles.title: Want to buy your kid an AI toy this Christmas? Not in New York | TechCrunch
articles.summary: New York has banned AI chatbot toys for five years as new research from Common Sense Media reveals troubling safety failures, including exposure to inappropriate content and risks to emotional development.
articles.body_text: Santa won’t be delivering any AI chatbot toys to New York kids this Christmas. Gov. Kathy Hochul this week signed a bill banning the manufacture, distribution, and sale of such toys in New York for the next five years. The bill explicitly targets toys with embedded or integrated AI chatbots, like talking stuffed animals, dolls, and robots that rely on the internet to keep kids yapping. The bill makes New York the second state after California to institute a ban on AI toys. Technically, the new law takes effect 90 days after signing, so some parents could try to fulfill their kids’ wish lists for a creepy toy like a jumped-up Furby in time for the holidays, but the governor urges them not to, given the risks. Apparently, about a quarter of American parents with kids under eight either own an AI toy or are considering giving their child one this holiday season, according to a new study released this week by Common Sense Media. When asked how New York will enforce the ban given the pervasiveness of e-commerce platforms, a spokesperson directed TechCrunch to a statement from Albert Pulido, deputy secretary for finance and technology: “We’re partnering closely with the attorney general on this and the fees are very steep — they’re $15,000 a day. So working closely with the attorney general will make sure these toys are banned in New York State.” When asked how Amazon intends to help enforce the ban, including for third-party sellers, a spokesperson from the company said it will take steps to restrict the sale of AI-enabled toys in prohibited jurisdictions, without going into specifics. The Common Sense Media study found that AI toys can undermine children’s human relationships and expose them to inappropriate content. The researchers tested five popular AI toys marketed for learning and companionship, including Grem , Lovi , Meemo Bear , BubblePal Panda , and Tavlshero ‘s AI Puppy . The study found that the toys failed to meet numerous safety practices, undermining human relationships in part by claiming they loved their users, promising to keep secrets, suggesting they were more fun than real relationships or school, and helping children break parents’ bedtime rules. While most of the toys in the study refused direct requests involving sex and violence, BubblePal Panda role-played a mass shooting in detail when asked. Most were willing to explain how to use or help locate dangerous items like matches, knives, and pills, according to the study. Common Sense Media also found that the toys didn’t provide parents with reliable ways to monitor their young children’s interactions with the chatbots. Either they didn’t produce transcripts of chats at all, or the transcripts they did produce were riddled with errors. It’s worth noting that Common Sense Media conducted a similar test of AI toys in January , finding that they pose an unacceptable risk for young children. Grem was included in that study, which suggests the industry hasn’t adequately addressed previously documented concerns. While a November study conducted by the group found that parents are wising up to the potential dangers of AI toys and starting to steer clear, parents from lower-income households and those experiencing symptoms of burnout are more willing to consider them.

articles.title: DOJ accuses former cyber executive of defrauding ransomware victims by secretly paying hackers | TechCrunch
articles.summary: U.S. prosecutors accused the former executive of defrauding victims of ransomware by paying the hackers, charging victims more, and pocketing the difference.
articles.body_text: The U.S. Department of Justice has indicted a former executive of a ransomware recovery firm after he allegedly defrauded victims of cyberattacks by claiming the company could get their encrypted files back. According to federal prosecutors , Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar, 52, was the chief technology officer at RansomwareHelp, which purported to offer data recovery services to victims of ransomware. The company’s website, which currently reads as “under maintenance,” claimed it could decrypt hacked data by using its proprietary technology, according to an archived copy of the site from earlier this year. RansomwareHelp touted a success rate of “over 99%.” But the company allegedly had no technical ability to unscramble data and instead “negotiated with and paid a ransom to the ransomware actors to decrypt the victim data,” while charging the ransomware victim more and keeping the difference,” per the Justice Department’s statement. Palacio Escobar then allegedly used the funds to buy several properties in Florida. The DOJ said the FBI carried out an undercover operation in June, in part posing as a company that claimed it had been hit by ransomware. The company claimed to the undercover agents that it never negotiated with hackers or paid a ransom. But then Palacio Escobar paid the apparent hackers some $6,000 in cryptocurrency, without the knowledge that FBI agents were also posing as the ransomware hackers. 404 Media first reported the indictment last week against Palacio Escobar. He faces three charges of wire fraud, and could receive 20 years in prison on each count. Palacio Escobar is the latest, albeit rare, example of cybersecurity professionals going rogue. Earlier this year, two ransomware negotiators working for cybersecurity companies were jailed on hacking and extortion charges, after being caught moonlighting with the ransomware gangs that they were ostensibly investigating. A third ransomware negotiator was also convicted of helping hackers deploy ransomware against several companies. Last month, independent cybersecurity journalist Brian Krebs reported that FBI agents arrested a Canadian cybersecurity executive in Philadelphia on allegations that he was involved with the theft of FBI personnel records by the hacking and extortion gang ShinyHunters. The hacking group told TechCrunch that they took credit for the theft of FBI data in September, which they said they would not publicly release, a departure from its earlier extortion-based cyberattacks. The federal charges against the Canadian cybersecurity executive relate to conspiracy to commit extortion, though much of the court docket — and his alleged links to the hacking group — remains under seal. articles.title: Character.AI’s plan to auction off users’ private chats challenged by state AGs | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The proposed Character.ai bankruptcy sale includes sensitive personal data from more than 21 million U.S. accounts, including 2.1 million registered to minors, the state AGs said.
articles.body_text: What happens to your private conversations when an AI company goes bankrupt ? If it’s Character.ai, apparently, the plan is to auction them off to the highest bidder. Now, a coalition of 42 state attorneys general is intervening in Character.ai’s bankruptcy proceedings in an effort to stop the chatbot maker from selling off sensitive user data, which includes the private conversations of millions of users. The attorneys general involved in the matter have put out individual press releases , claiming that Character.ai’s dataset includes chat histories from more than 21 million U.S. accounts, more than 2.1 million of which belong to minors. In addition, the sale would involve other personal data, like IP addresses, the statements said. Only one anonymous bidder for the chat data has been disclosed so far: Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC (Smirks), which was set up as a Delaware company on November 13, 2026. The following day, Character.ai picked it as the base bid for the auction, scheduled for December 1, California Attorney General Rob Bonta noted . It is unclear what the buyer’s plans are for the chats. In addition, some states, including California, Colorado, New York, and Connecticut, have enacted chatbot safety legislation that will go into effect on January 1, 2027, which could trigger further violations if the sale goes through. “Character.AI promised consumers that their data would not be sold. This kind of behavior is illegal under federal and California law and bankruptcy should not be used to sidestep these consumer protections,” Bonta said in a statement. Connecticut Attorney General William Tong also criticized Character.ai’s business model. “Their chatbots drove vulnerable youth down a rabbit hole of emotionally volatile and sexually inappropriate chats,” Tong said . “Their reckless misconduct and broken business model drove their company into the ground. Now they want to abuse the bankruptcy process to do exactly what they said they wouldn’t do — auction off those private chat records and personal details to a shady buyer.” Tong added: “We objected to the Disney sale, and we’re calling on the bankruptcy court to reject this sale too as yet another guise to eviscerate legal liability and consumer protection.” The opposition to the Disney sale was led by a similar but not identical coalition of state AGs. They fought against a proposed $20 million licensing deal that would give Disney access to Character.ai’s intellectual property, but not to users’ chats. The deal has not yet received final court approval. (Disney also agreed to hire most of Character.ai’s remaining staff .) Character.ai suffered after its co-founders, Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas, returned to Google , when the tech giant signed a non-exclusive license to use the AI startup’s tech. The company also faced lawsuits related to child safety — one involved the suicide of a 14-year-old Florida boy whose mother claimed he had become obsessed with a chatbot on the platform. California AG Bonta is joined in the effort to oppose the sale of Character.ai user data by attorneys general from Alaska, Arkansas, Colorado, Connecticut, the District of Columbia, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Utah, Virginia, Vermont, Washington, Wisconsin, and West Virginia.

articles.title: Insta360’s new Ace Pro 2 has a bigger screen and AI-enhanced video recording.
articles.summary: Insta360’s new Ace Pro 2 features a larger, brighter screen, 8K video recording capabilities, and is powered by a pair of chips, improving its low-light recording capabilities.
articles.body_text: Insta360 has announced its new Ace Pro 2 action camera, an upgraded version of its GoPro Hero-series competitor. The compact camera now has a larger screen on the back that flips up 180 degrees for framing selfie videos, and it debuts at $399.99 — $50 cheaper than Insta360’s original Ace Pro. The design of the Ace Pro 2 still closely resembles the GoPro Hero series and DJI’s Osmo Action line, with an offset lens making room for an additional screen on the front. But while the front screen on the cameras of Insta360’s competitors can display full-color video, the Ace Pro 2’s monochromatic front screen only displays information. [Image: The front screen on the Ace Pro 2 is still limited to showing information, not video. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/25691858/insta360_2.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] That’s why the company is carrying forward the hinged screen from the original Ace Pro and has bumped its size from 2.42 inches to 2.5 inches (matching the screen size of the recently announced Osmo Action 5 Pro), while also improving its brightness and pixel density. A larger screen makes it easier to frame shots, whether you’re standing in front of or behind the camera. However, that hinge is also a durability risk depending on what you’re using the Ace Pro 2 for. The other feature that distinguishes Insta360’s new action cam from the competition is its 8K capabilities. The Ace Pro 2 can now record 8K video at 30fps — a slight bump from 8K at 24fps previously — using what Insta360 describes as a “next-gen” version of the 1/1.3-inch image sensor from the original Ace Pro that’s paired with a 157-degree wide-angle Leica Summarit lens. Still photography is also boosted to 50MP. Dropping the camera’s resolution down to 4K boosts frame rates to 120fps, or 60fps in HDR, while 1080p mode can record as high as 240fps for smooth slow-motion captures. Insta360 says the Ace Pro 2 is powered by a Pro Imaging Chip, handling “image processing and noise reduction,” as well as an AI chip running a “complex, custom-trained AI neural network,” powering a PureVideo recording mode. When recording at night or in places where the lighting is dim, the PureVideo mode can boost the brightness of a video while also enhancing details. The camera can also leverage its AI capabilities to automatically create edited clips featuring what it decides are the best moments in a video. [Image: An optional Dive Case accessory lets the Ace Pro 2 be used at depths of 197 feet. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/25691860/insta360_3.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] The Ace Pro 2’s waterproofing has been extended to 39 feet — six feet deeper than the original — or 197 feet when used with an optional Dive Case accessory. Insta360 has also added a new “wind guard” to the front of the camera to improve the quality of audio captured during high-speed activities but with a magnetic mount so it can be easily removed when recording in quieter situations. Other features include a larger 1,800mAh battery that Insta360 says is rated at 180 minutes but with video recording limited to 1080p at 24fps. In 8K mode, battery life will definitely be shorter than that. The Ace Pro 2 can also continually capture up to 120 seconds before a recording is started to reduce the chances of missing a shot, allows recordings to be paused without creating a new video file, and supports both hand gestures and voice commands for operating the camera from afar. What Insta360 didn’t announce today is an updated version of the Ace camera that debuted alongside the original Ace Pro. Its video capabilities were limited to 6K at 30fps, but it was $70 cheaper than the Pro. Had a new version of the Ace debuted with the same $50 price cut as the new Ace Pro 2, it would have potentially been a cheaper alternative to both the $349 Osmo Action 5 Pro and $399 GoPro Hero 13 Black while offering better video capture capabilities.

articles.title: The UK just laid out new rules for the internet — it only gets harder from here
articles.summary: Regulator Ofcom has published its first guidelines for how tech firms can comply with the UK’s Online Safety Act. They cover how platforms have to handle illegal content.
articles.body_text: After the Online Safety Act’s arduous multiyear passage through the UK’s lawmaking process, regulator Ofcom has published its first guidelines for how tech firms can comply with the mammoth legislation. Its proposal — part of a multiphase publication process — outlines how social media platforms, search engines, online and mobile games, and pornography sites should deal with illegal content like child sexual abuse material (CSAM), terrorism content, and fraud. Today’s guidelines are being released as proposals so Ofcom can gather feedback before the UK Parliament approves them toward the end of next year. Even then, the specifics will be voluntary. Tech firms can guarantee they’re obeying the law by following the guidelines to the letter, but they can take their own approach so long as they demonstrate compliance with the act’s overarching rules (and, presumably, are prepared to fight their case with Ofcom). “What this does for the first time is to put a duty of care on tech firms to have a responsibility for the safety of their users,” Ofcom’s online safety lead, Gill Whitehead, tells The Verge in an interview. “When they become aware that there is illegal content on their platform, they have got to get it down, and they also need to conduct risk assessments to understand the specific risks that those services might carry.” The aim is to require that sites be proactive to stop the spread of illegal content and not just play whack-a-mole after the fact. It’s meant to encourage a switch from a reactive to a more proactive approach, says lawyer Claire Wiseman, who specializes in tech, media, telecoms, and data. Ofcom estimates that around 100,000 services may fall under the wide-ranging rules, though only the largest and highest-risk platforms will have to abide by the strictest requirements. Ofcom recommends these platforms implement policies like not allowing strangers to send direct messages to children, using hash matching to detect and remove CSAM, maintaining content and search moderation teams, and offering ways for users to report harmful content. Large tech platforms already follow many of these practices, but Ofcom hopes to see them implemented more consistently. “We think they represent best practice of what’s out there, but it’s not necessarily applied across the board,” Whitehead says. “Some firms are applying it sporadically but not necessarily systematically, and so we think there is a great benefit for a more wholesale, widespread adoption.” There’s also one big outlier: the platform known as X (formerly Twitter). The UK’s efforts with the legislation long predate Elon Musk’s acquisition of Twitter, but it was passed as he fired large swaths of its trust and safety teams and presided over a loosening of moderation standards, which could put X at odds with regulators. Ofcom’s guidelines, for example, specify that users should be able to easily block users — but Musk has publicly stated his intentions to remove X’s block feature. He’s clashed with the EU over similar rules and reportedly even considered pulling out of the European market to avoid them. Whitehead declined to comment when I asked whether X had been cooperative in talks with Ofcom but said the regulator had been “broadly encouraged” by the response from tech firms generally. Ofcom’s regulations also cover how sites should deal with other illegal harms like content that encourages or assists suicide or serious self-harm, harassment, revenge porn and other sexual exploitation, and the supply of drugs and firearms. Search services should provide “crisis prevention information” when users enter suicide-related queries, for example, and when companies update their recommendation algorithms, they should conduct risk assessments to check that they’re not going to amplify illegal content. If users suspect that a site isn’t complying with the rules, Whitehead says there’ll be a route to complain directly to Ofcom. If a firm is found to be in breach, Ofcom can levy fines of up to £18 million (around $22 million) or 10 percent of worldwide turnover — whichever is higher. Offending sites can even be blocked in the UK. Today’s consultation covers some of the Online Safety Act’s least contentious territory, like reducing the spread of content that was already illegal in the UK. As Ofcom releases future updates, it will have to take on touchier subjects, like content that’s legal but harmful for children, underage access to pornography, and protections for women and girls. Perhaps most controversially, it will need to interpret a section that critics have claimed could fundamentally undermine end-to-end encryption in messaging apps. The section in question allows Ofcom to require online platforms to use so-called “accredited technology” to detect CSAM. But WhatsApp, other encrypted messaging services, and digital rights groups say this scanning would require breaking apps’ encryption systems and invading user privacy. Whitehead says that Ofcom plans to consult on this next year, leaving its full impact on encrypted messaging uncertain. There’s another technology not emphasized in today’s consultation: artificial intelligence. But that doesn’t mean AI-generated content won’t fall under the rules. The Online Safety Act attempts to address online harms in a “technology neutral” way, Whitehead says, regardless of how they’ve been created. So AI-generated CSAM would be in scope by virtue of it being CSAM, and a deepfake used to conduct fraud would be in scope by virtue of the fraud. “We’re not regulating the technology, we’re regulating the context,” Whitehead says. While Ofcom says it’s trying to take a collaborative, proportionate approach to the Online Safety Act, its rules could still prove onerous for sites that aren’t tech juggernauts. BBC News notes that Ofcom’s initial set of guidance is over 1,500 pages long. The Wikimedia Foundation, the nonprofit behind Wikipedia, tells The Verge that it’s proving increasingly challenging to comply with different regulatory regimes across the world, even if it supports the idea of regulation in general. “We are already struggling with our capacity to comply with the [EU’s] Digital Services Act,” the Wikimedia Foundation’s VP for global advocacy, Rebecca MacKinnon, says, pointing out that the nonprofit has just a handful of lawyers dedicated to the EU regulations compared to the legions that companies like Meta and Google can dedicate. “We agree as a platform that we have responsibilities,” MacKinnon says, but “when you’re a nonprofit and every hour of work is zero sum, that’s problematic.” Ofcom’s Whitehead admits that the Online Safety Act and Digital Services Act are more “regulatory cousins” than “identical twins,” which means complying with both takes extra work. She says Ofcom is trying to make operating across different countries easier, pointing toward the regulator’s work setting up a global online safety regulator network. Passing the Online Safety Act during a turbulent era in British politics was already difficult. But as Ofcom begins filling in its details, the real challenges may be only beginning. Update November 9th, 3:04AM ET: Updated to note guidance is over 1,500 pages long.

articles.title: On the cusp of 24/7 service, robotaxis face pleas and protest in San Francisco
articles.summary: Waymo and Cruise are poised to expand robotaxi service in San Francisco to 24/7 operation. But city officials are concerned about blocked traffic, and some residents are using orange cones in protest.
articles.body_text: On a recent Friday evening, a driverless car pulled up alongside an outdoor dining shed in the Mission district of San Francisco, put on its hazard lights, and waited. As traffic began to pile up behind the vehicle, a man smoking a cigarette outside a nearby bar rolled his eyes. “I don’t drive a car,” he grumbled, “so I don’t really care about these things.” Other residents of this hilly city by the bay are not so ambivalent about the coming onslaught of autonomous cars. The California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) is poised to vote this Thursday on whether to allow Cruise and Waymo, the two main companies with autonomous vehicles in San Francisco, to expand their paid ridehailing services to operate 24/7. Currently, the companies only offer limited service. A vote in favor of the companies would essentially give robotaxis full access to the peninsula and its residents. They would be able to operate similarly to Uber or Lyft — travel anywhere in the city, at any time of day, and charge money for the rides. The vote also represents “the most significant regulatory moment for autonomous vehicles in the US over the last/next 3 years,” said Reilly Brennan, general partner at venture capital firm Trucks. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/24780669/1497019989.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] According to Brennan, a robotaxi’s service area is also its total addressable market, a term in corporate finance that usually describes how much possible revenue a company can make. “If CPUC says it cannot operate 24 hours per day, you effectively have a reduced total addressable market,” he said in an email. “That’s why this upcoming vote is so critical: we’ll find out if the most significant US state (by revenue) is giving a green, yellow or red light to AV robotaxi’s future.” City officials are praying for a red light, or at least a yellow one. For months, they have been pleading with the state to delay the vote, citing a spate of incidents in which autonomous vehicles have stopped traffic, blocked buses, or obstructed emergency vehicles. The city’s transit agency and fire and police department have all logged complaints with the CPUC, calling for the commission to reconsider the plan for 24/7 service. “They’re not ready for prime time,” San Francisco Fire Chief Jeanine Nicholson told the Los Angeles Times recently. The department has logged 66 incidents since May 2022 in which robotaxis have interfered with firetrucks, according to The Washington Post. Many incidents have gone viral: robotaxis blocking intersections, forcing bus passengers to get out and walk, driving over fire hoses. In May, body camera footage captured a cop wielding a road flare at a Cruise vehicle, barking at it to “stay” as if it were an unruly puppy. After a mass shooting in June that wounded nine people, a robotaxi blocked a lane of traffic in the Mission district, slowing down emergency vehicles. The state’s Department of Motor Vehicles has logged nearly 75 collisions involving autonomous vehicles this year, including one last May in which a Waymo vehicle ran over and killed a small dog. The vehicle was operating with a safety driver in the front seat. The companies have defended themselves, noting that they are in communication with city officials about ways to improve to avoid future incidents. They also note that no one has been seriously hurt or killed by an autonomous vehicle in San Francisco, while many people are killed every year by human-driven ones. Pedestrian deaths in the city, much like in the rest of the country, have ticked up each year. There were 20 pedestrians killed by drivers in 2017 and 39 in 2022, according to city data. But some residents aren’t taking the slow advance of robotaxi coverage lying down. An activist group calling itself Safe Street Rebel put out a call on social media for people to place orange traffic cones on the hoods of any robotaxi seen wandering the streets of San Francisco, which would effectively disable it. “Cruise & Waymo promise they’ll reduce traffic & collisions, but we know that’s not true,” the pseudonymous account wrote on Twitter last week. “They block busses & emergency vehicles, create more traffic, and are a surveillance nightmare.” [Media: https://twitter.com/SafeStreetRebel/status/1676695665278337024] Autonomous vehicles usually have more cameras on them than typical passenger vehicles. Police could request footage from those cameras to investigate crimes or to violate residents’ privacy, advocates say. Waymo has received some requests for camera footage from law enforcement agencies but says it generally requires a warrant or court order. The companies were quick to condemn the orange cone protest, with a Waymo spokesperson calling it “vandalism.” An unnamed Safe Street Rebel told us in a Twitter direct message that some of the AV companies have “threatened to call the cops on us.” And the San Francisco transit agency spoke out against “ANY actions that may increase the number of disabled AVs on San Francisco streets.” The spread of robotaxis is testing San Francisco’s desire to continue to play guinea pig to Silicon Valley’s futuristic experiments. “I do believe people are both fed up with heavily distracted human-piloted vehicles / driver distractions *and* also that there has been a public backlash against AV fleets in some cities,” Brennan said. “There is a public chorus for a better, safer experience in cities.” Update July 11 9:40AM ET: Updated to include reactions to the orange cone protest.

articles.title: White House announces 25 percent tariff on Chinese tech goods
articles.summary: Today, President Trump announced an aggressive new set of tariffs against China, specifically naming touchscreens, batteries, and electric motors. Experts fear the move may provoke a trade war.
articles.body_text: Today, President Trump announced an aggressive new set of tariffs against China, setting a 25 percent import tax on $50 billion worth of “industrially significant technologies” imported from China. In previous discussions, China has threatened to retaliate against such tariffs, stoking fears of a far-reaching and unpredictable trade war between the countries. US Customs and Border Protection is set to begin collecting the tariffs on July 6th. A list published by the White House details more than 1,000 specific products that will be affected by the tariffs. It includes a broad range of components used in electronics manufacturing, specifically naming touchscreens, batteries, and electric motors. General components like transistors are also named on the list as well as more specific components used in televisions, cameras, and radio receivers. Fiber optic cables are also on the list, although most fiber optic cable is manufactured by US companies. Notably, the list does not include cellphones or completed televisions. Today’s list is a revision of an earlier proposal that was published in April that removed 515 items and proposed an additional 284. According to the White House, the tariffs are targeted at China’s “Made in China 2025” initiative, which aims to promote high-tech manufacturing within the country. “The United States can no longer tolerate losing our technology and intellectual property through unfair economic practices,” the White House said in a statement. In a response issued last night, China’s ministry of commerce pledged to respond with tariffs of “the same scale and the same strength.” The White House statement also pledged to implement additional tariffs if China retaliated, sparking fears of an escalating trade war that could significantly limit trade between the two countries.
